title: Operations, Debugging And Incident Leadership Checkpoint

questions.prompt: An API is fast but users see stale shipment status. Which conclusion follows?

options.label: Latency alone does not measure the useful customer outcome or source freshness.
The workflow is healthy because the server is responding.
The UI should hide timestamps to reduce concern.

questions.explanation: Infrastructure responsiveness is one indicator. Freshness and task correctness need separate evidence; hiding uncertainty makes the experience less trustworthy.

questions.prompt: During a stale-data incident, what should happen while the cause is investigated?

options.label: Keep showing data as current until a root cause is certain.
Promise complete recovery based only on a service restart.
Contain harm, expose freshness, offer the approved fallback and communicate known impact.

questions.explanation: Mitigation and investigation can proceed together. Mislabeling stale data prolongs harm, and restart is not proof of recovered user behavior.

questions.prompt: How should a trace help investigate a customer failure?

options.label: Remove all operation IDs so no one can connect events.
Correlate safe operation metadata while minimizing sensitive payloads.
Copy every customer document into unrestricted logs.

questions.explanation: Useful correlation does not require unrestricted content capture. Overcollection exposes data; removing all correlation makes diagnosis harder.

questions.prompt: Which evidence supports a recovery claim after an exporter incident?

options.label: Fresh source data and successful affected user workflows over the agreed observation window.
A green unit-test run without checking the affected system.
A confident message from someone who has not observed the workflow.

questions.explanation: Recovery requires observation at the failed boundary and user journey. Test success and confidence do not establish restored service.
